primaryUsageEvidence.point: Collins explicitly gives stretch your wings as an alternate to spread your wings.
Cambridge records think straight for clear thinking; source comparative think straighter needs separate editorial support.
Cambridge records an object-flexible shine-off idiom, but does not resolve source 3468 pronoun reference.
Cambridge supports spreading downstream effects; causative send ripples still needs its own bounded grammar gate.

rows.sourceSentence: One policy change can send ripples far beyond the office.
rows.senseAndBoundary: Same spreading-consequences decision as 772; however send ripples is causative noun construction, while owner teaches intransitive ripple out/through. A bounded alternate can be considered if its grammar is explained and assessed, not silently folded into the verb pattern.
rows.nextGate: Add a branch requiring send/sends/sent/sending + ripples + a path/extent complement; exclude literal water ripples and standalone far beyond. Test full source plus existing 772 positives.

rows.sourceSentence: Creativity changes its clothes as people grow older.
rows.senseAndBoundary: Same underlying-form-change image as 1706, but changes its clothes is a productive personification, not established as a reusable fixed unit by this source alone. Current owner teaches the narrower has simply changed clothes form.
rows.nextGate: If later promoted, handle with 3753 and 3998 together; require semantic evidence, bounded abstract subject and nonliteral use.

rows.sourceSentence: A calm conversation helped me think straighter.
rows.senseAndBoundary: Source comparative think straighter conveys clarity but is less conventional than the documented think straight unit. Broadly adding straighter would teach an uncertain form, with no unique learner decision.
rows.nextGate: Editorially normalize source example or retain hold; do not claim the current 873 detector covers it.

rows.sourceSentence: A good mentor is a bit like a compass.
rows.senseAndBoundary: A mentor is a bit like a compass is a transparent productive simile. Owner 1913 already teaches a mentor acting like a compass; new wording adds no distinct reusable target.
rows.nextGate: Retain the source as contextual example only if prose provenance is desired; do not widen assessment detector to any like a compass string.

rows.sourceSentence: Pressure can make advice feel like a cage rather than a compass.
rows.senseAndBoundary: Owner 904 already contrasts direction with over-control and supports a comparative variant. Source reverses the evaluation but tests the same learner decision: pressure turns advice into a restriction rather than guidance.
rows.nextGate: If expanding, require the complete paired cage/compass comparison, preserve direction of contrast, add Chinese/answer check; reject cage or compass alone.

rows.sourceSentence: A long journey can take the shine off it.
rows.currentOwnerTargetPattern: \btak(?:e|es|en|ing) the shine off the trip\b|\btook the shine off the trip\b
rows.senseAndBoundary: The established idiom can take varied objects, but this source’s it has no clear antecedent. Owner 1839 is trip-specific; importing the ambiguous pronoun would make its answer evidence weak.
rows.nextGate: Clarify original referent in source metadata or use a verified sentence before broadening trip-only owner.

rows.sourceSentence: Parents need not be holding the steering wheel all the time.
rows.senseAndBoundary: Control metaphor is semantically close to 2876, yet holding the steering wheel all the time is productive imagery rather than its hands-on-the-wheel unit. Widening the detector would risk literal driving and a second lesson grammar.
rows.nextGate: Hold until a distinct reusable construction and target boundary are justified; do not equate wheel noun alone with practical authority.

rows.sourceSentence: Teenagers need safe chances to stretch their wings.
rows.senseAndBoundary: Collins explicitly lists stretch your wings as an alternate to spread your wings. Source safe chances for teenagers to gain independence fits owner 2055, without requiring a second lesson.
rows.nextGate: Add stretch/stretches/stretched/stretching + possessive + wings as a separate bounded branch; require figurative development context in assessment, keep literal bird/body examples negative.

rows.sourceSentence: The habit changed its clothes when it moved online.
rows.senseAndBoundary: Different form of the same clothing personification as 3031, but presently a bespoke metaphor. Exact source-sense overlap does not by itself justify target expansion.
rows.nextGate: Resolve together with 3031 and repeated 3998, not as a new owner.

rows.sourceSentence: The programme is deeply woven into community life.
rows.currentOwnerTargetPattern: (?:\b(?:deeply )?woven into (?:daily routines|(?:ordinary )?daily life|ordinary life|everyday living|everyday life)\b)|(?:\bwoven quite naturally into everyday life\b)
rows.senseAndBoundary: Community life describes social integration, broader than owner 1503’s habitual daily routines. Canonical 271 covers community fabric but requires woven into the fabric; this source omits fabric. Neither detector safely owns it today.
rows.nextGate: Keep held pending proof of routine frequency or a separately justified bounded community-life unit; do not auto-route to 1503/271.

rows.sourceSentence: Creativity changes its clothes as people grow older.
rows.senseAndBoundary: Exact repeat of 3031 source sentence. It should inherit 3031’s eventual disposition, not spawn a separate lesson.
rows.nextGate: Keep held until 3031 is resolved; then attach repeat occurrence as source provenance only.
